entries.originalText: “My Son, patience and humility in adversities are more pleasing to Me than much comfort and devotion in prosperity.
entries.modernizedText: “My Son, patience and humility in adversity are more pleasing to Me than much comfort and devotion in prosperity.

entries.originalText: Why doth a little thing spoken against thee make thee sad?
entries.modernizedText: Why does a little thing spoken against you make you sad?

entries.originalText: If it had been more, thou still oughtest not to be moved.
entries.modernizedText: Even if it had been more, you ought not to be moved.

entries.originalText: But now suffer it to go by; it is not the first, it is not new, and it will not be the last, if thou live long.
entries.modernizedText: But now let it pass; it is not the first, it is not new, and it will not be the last if you live long.

entries.originalText: Thou art brave enough, so long as no adversity meeteth thee.
entries.modernizedText: You are brave enough as long as no adversity meets you.

entries.originalText: Thou givest good counsel also, and knowest how to strengthen others with thy words; but when tribulation suddenly knocketh at thine own door, thy counsel and strength fail.
entries.modernizedText: You also give good counsel and know how to strengthen others with your words; but when trouble suddenly knocks at your own door, your counsel and strength fail.

entries.originalText: Consider thy great frailty, which thou dost so often experience in trifling matters nevertheless, for thy soul’s health these things are done when they and such like happen unto thee.
entries.modernizedText: Consider your great frailty, which you so often experience in trifling matters; nevertheless, when these and similar things happen to you, they are done for the health of your soul.

entries.originalText: “Put them away from thy heart as well as thou canst, and if tribulation hath touched thee, yet let it not cast thee down nor entangle thee long.
entries.modernizedText: “Put them away from your heart as well as you can, and if trouble has touched you, do not let it cast you down or entangle you for long.

entries.originalText: At the least, bear patiently, if thou canst not joyfully.
entries.modernizedText: At least bear it patiently, if you cannot do so joyfully.

entries.originalText: And although thou be very unwilling to hear it, and feel indignation, yet check thyself, and suffer no unadvised word to come forth from thy lips, whereby the little ones may be offended.
entries.modernizedText: And although you are very unwilling to hear it and feel indignation, check yourself and allow no careless word to come from your lips by which the little ones may be offended.

entries.originalText: Soon the storm which hath been raised shall be stilled, and inward grief shall be sweetened by returning grace.
entries.modernizedText: Soon the storm that has arisen will be stilled, and inward grief will be sweetened by returning grace.

entries.originalText: I yet live, saith the Lord, ready to help thee, and to give thee more than wonted consolation if thou put thy trust in Me, and call devoutly upon Me.
entries.modernizedText: I still live, says the Lord, ready to help you and give you more than usual consolation if you put your trust in Me and call devoutly upon Me.

entries.originalText: “Be thou more calm of spirit, and gird thyself for greater endurance.
entries.modernizedText: “Be calmer in spirit and prepare yourself for greater endurance.

entries.originalText: All is not frustrated, though thou find thyself very often afflicted or grievously tempted.
entries.modernizedText: All is not frustrated, though you find yourself very often afflicted or grievously tempted.

entries.originalText: Thou art man, not God; thou art flesh, not an angel.
entries.modernizedText: You are human, not God; you are flesh, not an angel.

entries.originalText: How shouldst thou be able to remain alway in the same state of virtue, when an angel in heaven fell, and the first man in paradise?
entries.modernizedText: How could you remain always in the same state of virtue when an angel in heaven fell, and the first man in paradise?

entries.originalText: I am He who lifteth up the mourners to deliverance, and those who know their own infirmity I raise up to my own nature.”
entries.modernizedText: I am He who lifts up mourners to deliverance, and those who know their own weakness I raise up to My own nature.”

entries.originalText: O Lord, blessed be Thy word, sweeter to my mouth than honey and the honeycomb.
entries.modernizedText: O Lord, blessed be Your word, sweeter to my mouth than honey and the honeycomb.

entries.originalText: What should I do in my so great tribulations and anxieties, unless Thou didst comfort me with Thy holy words?
entries.modernizedText: What would I do in my great troubles and anxieties unless You comforted me with Your holy words?

entries.originalText: If only I may attain unto the haven of salvation, what matter is it what things or how many I suffer?
entries.modernizedText: If only I may reach the haven of salvation, what does it matter what or how much I suffer?

entries.originalText: Give me a good end, give me a happy passage out of this world.
entries.modernizedText: Give me a good end; give me a happy passage out of this world.

entries.originalText: Remember me, O my God, and lead me by the right way unto Thy Kingdom.
entries.modernizedText: Remember me, O my God, and lead me by the right way to Your Kingdom.

entries.originalText: Amen.
entries.modernizedText: Amen.
